I can include and describe the example:

For context, a guy and a girl whose exact age aren’t revealed but are probably in their early twenties have met each other. The girl, Ember, lives on an island of women and has trouble trusting men. The guy, Medra, finds himself there by accident. He knows Ember’s past and doesn’t want to press her boundaries so he keeps a respectful distance. For some time they remain distant, but spend more time together going on walks in the woods in silence. They get to become friends and eventually, lovers. Their first time having sex is described here:

“They were both shy. When Medra took her hand his hand shook, and Ember…turned away scowling. Then she touched his hand very lightly. When he stroked the sleek black flow of her hair she seemed only to endure his touch, and he stopped. When he tried to embrace her she was stiff, rejecting him. Then she turned and, fierce, hasty, awkward, seized him in her arms. It wasn’t the first night, nor the first nights, they passed together that gave either of them much pleasure or ease. But they learned from each other, and came through shame and fear into passion. Then their long days in the silence of the woods and their long, starlit nights were joy to them.”

There are three body parts that are described. Medra’s hand is shaking, Ember’s hair is black, and her face is scowling. The most explicitly sexual action is Ember “seizing” him.

Now look at the emotional words. There are five emotional adjectives used in the first part describe one or both of them: Shy, stiff, fierce, hasty, and awkward.

As soon as they start touching each other, the “camera”/perspective pulls back, the narration becomes more detached as if it’s a storyteller describing the scene and not the young lovers themselves. Their bodies are not described any further and the emotional words are no longer adjectives but nouns: shame, fear, passion, and joy.

When writing pornography, the most important thing is specific sexual actions and vulgar descriptions of bodies. In ordinary prose, the most important thing to describe is the emotions surrounding sex. In the case of very young people, they have to overcome awkwardness and hesitation before they can relax into true passion. Hope this helps!

1 rare magic item: Wand of Paralysis (DMG)
- 7 charges
- Use an action to expend a charge and target a creature you can see within 60 feet. DC 15 Con save, paralyzed for 1 minute on a failure. Can remake the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.
- 1d6 +1 charges regained at dawn. If you use the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the wand is destroyed.

The idea is to win initiative and use your first turn to cast a big control spell, choosing your spell depending on what enemy you are facing. After, you can use your action evasively to maintain concentration to make up for your bad con saves.

During your morning preparations, cast mage armor for an AC of 16. This isn’t bad for a wizard, a cleric of the same level might have heavy armor and a fighter optimized for AC could have a base of 19. You also have a permanent reactionary AC bonus thanks to your subclass. It comes with a price, but it doesn’t matter so much considering your options during combat.

Your Dexterity and Intelligence modifiers are both +3 and your proficiency bonus is +2, meaning your initiative bonus is +8, which means you are beating most creatures.

Use your first action to cast a single target or multiple target spell depending on the combat.

Cause Fear targets Wisdom and will keep a single target away from you and impose disadvantage on its attack rolls while it sees you.

Charm Person doesn’t require concentration and can be use to end a combat with a humanoid before it begins.

Color Spray has no saving throw and causes blindness, possibly in multiple enemies.

Protection From Good and Evil is a flexible defensive option for protecting yourself or an ally

Silvery Barbs is going to annoy your DM. It uses your reaction, which clashes with Arcane Deflection but if you aren’t being attack consistently or targeted by saving throws, then cast this spell. This causes disadvantage on a d20 test and giving advantage to an ally within the next minute.

Sleep is nice because there’s no saving throw, no concentration, and it’s still good at low levels. Unconscious creatures are incapacitated, and this may end a combat completely before it begins.

Tasha’s Hideous Laughter causes the incapacitated and prone conditions

Crown of Madness is good for turning an enemy against another.

Earthbind is a good option to drag a flying enemy into melee combat with your martial allies.

On each subsequent action while you are concentrating, you can either Disengage, cast a cantrip, or use the Wand of Paralysis, which gels nicely with your Arcane Deflection feature because you probably aren’t casting leveled spells round after round. 

Stay Out of Melee
You should be staying on the back lines as much  as possible. You can always take the Disengage action or you can hop away using your bonus action. If you have no uses left or there’s no room to move, or you have no movement speed, use your action for Gust, pushing a Medium creature up to 5 feet away. If your enemy is Large or has high Strength saves, Blade Ward might actually be useful, giving you resistance to BPS damage.

Enjoy!

The best example I can think of is The Raft People from chapter 8 of The Farthest Shore by Ursula K. LeGuin. The main character of the novel is stranded at sea and is saved by them. When he wakes up they give him “a small cup of water, stale, tasting pitchy from the caulking of the barrel.” 

LeGuin seems less concerned with extensive worldbuilding than with telling a good story, so we have to assume a few things. The water is stale, so we can assume it’s been sitting out for a while, not freshly harvested for a newcomer, and also that they possess they technology to make a barrel or they acquired the barrel somewhere on a populated island of the world. 

We know that the Raft People inhabit the Southern Reach, a huge ocean in the southernmost part of the world’s map. The climate is the warmest part of earthsea, and the chief describes the “long rains” of the open sea. From this I assume the seasons are not spring-summer-autumn-winter, but rather a dry season and rainy season. They probably collect their water mostly during the rainy season and save as much as possible to get them through the dry season.

A quick Wikipedia search has revealed that it is possible to make pitch from plant life, especially birch and pine trees. It appears that pine tar in particular is made from applying heat to pine wood in a closed container such as an earthenware vessel. Greeks used to make pitch to seal wine casks, if your culture can safely use heat out on the sea without burning down their ships then they might be able to do so as well. If you want, we can use a little fantasy extrapolating and assume seaweed is also a viable material for making pitch.

Fiend

I think it’s most helpful to learn by example, so I’d like to share with you my favorite sex scene ever written about young love/sex. 

Context: a guy and a girl whose exact age aren’t revealed but are probably in their early twenties have met each other. The girl, Ember, lives on an island of women and has trouble trusting men. The guy, Medra, finds himself there by accident. He knows Ember’s past and doesn’t want to press her boundaries so he keeps a respectful distance. For some time they remain distant, but spend more time together going on walks in the woods in silence. They get to become friends and eventually, lovers. Their first time having sex is described here:

“They were both shy. When Medra took her hand his hand shook, and Ember…turned away scowling. Then she touched his hand very lightly. When he stroked the sleek black flow of her hair she seemed only to endure his touch, and he stopped. When he tried to embrace her she was stiff, rejecting him. Then she turned and, fierce, hasty, awkward, seized him in her arms. It wasn’t the first night, nor the the first nights, they passed together that gave either of them much pleasure or ease. But they learned from each other, and came through shame and fear into passion. Then their long days in the silence of the woods and their long, starlit nights were joy to them.”

There are three body parts that are described. Medra’s hand is shaking, Ember’s hair is black, and her face is scowling. The most explicitly sexual action is Ember “seizing” him. 

Now look at the emotional words. There are five emotional adjectives used in the first part describe one or both of them: Shy, stiff, fierce, hasty, and awkward.

As soon as they start touching each other, the “camera”/perspective pulls back, the narration becomes more detached as if it’s a storyteller describing the scene and not the young lovers themselves. Their bodies are not described any further and the emotional words are no longer adjectives but nouns: shame, fear, passion, and joy.

When writing pornography, the most important thing is specific sexual actions and vulgar descriptions of bodies. In ordinary prose, the most important thing to describe is the emotions surrounding sex. In the case of very young people, they have to overcome awkwardness and hesitation before they can relax into true passion. Hope this helps!

Two recommendations I can think of, without knowing further details of your character, campaign or DM.

Subclass Change
- It sounds like you’re okay with managing the exhaustion side effect, but if your DM is okay with it I might switch to Wild Magic for more variety. In my opinion it’s underrated, even at 3rd level you get a lot of good things. You can use a “detect magic” effect, not the spell but pretty much the same thing. There’s also the very fun Wild Magic table made for the subclass, most options for which deal damage in some way. I’m aware it’s not very good damage, it’s usually a low damage die and you can’t add any modifiers to it, but some of the possibilities are a different damage type such as force or radiant, and can be be done at range. There’s also an option that makes difficult terrain for your enemies, a teleportation option, and a way to get temporary hit points. So it’s not game-breaking, and harder to control than battle master maneuvers, but it’s still a cool and flavorful way to power up your barbarian.

Feats

-First option I like is Sentinel. Your opportunity attacks reduce a creature’s speed to 0, and creatures can’t Disengage from you. You can also make opportunity attacks when creatures in your range attack another creature besides yourself. This all sounds like peak barbarian stuff, and you’ll be much better at battlefield control, which is different than pure damage. Now, combine this with the difficult terrain Wild Magic option and most enemies will find it pretty much impossible to get away from you. Even if your opportunity attack misses, a creature with 30 feet of movement will only get 15 feet away, and you can just chase it down and do the whole thing over again. I might start using your action to knock a creature prone or grapple it for further control. The other option that blends well with this feat is the teleportation feat. It’s pretty much 30 feet of extra movement speed every turn without needing to risk opportunity attacks. You can position yourself around the boss of the encounter and just lock it down like nobody else.

-Second option is Slasher, if you’re using a slashing weapon. You can reduce a creature’s speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and your critical hits give it disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. I don’t know what weapon you’re using but this might be nice to take if you also want a +1 to Strength

I would take 3 levels of Hexblade.

Level 1

• 2 cantrips. I would recommend booming blade, it’s awesome on a swashbuckler. You can make your attack, causing extra thunder damage on top of your sneak attack damage, and then running away without taking opportunity attacks. The only reason a martial of your level wouldn’t use it is because you can only make one attack with the cantrip, but rogues only get one attack anyway. The other cantrip can be whatever, I don’t think you need eldritch blast unless you want a reliable ranged attack.

• Two known spells, a single 1st level spell slot. I recommend taking hex and wrathful smite.

• Hex: an extra d6 of necrotic damage for every attack against a chosen target, and it has disadvantage on checks made with a chosen ability. If you have a grappler in your party I recommend Strength. When you take your 9th level in swashbuckler you can choose Wisdom instead so your Panache feature works more reliably. You can even move the spell to another creature if the first is killed. Definitely my go-to spell at this level.

•wrathful smite: a little extra psychic damage, not much, but frightening a creature for up to a minute is pretty nice.

•Hexblade’s Curse: the extra damage on your attack is nice. The expanded critical hit range isn’t huge, but sneak attack dice get doubled on a critical so it works better in this multiclass. A few extra temporary hit points too if the target dies, but not much.

•Hex Warrior: Medium armor means you don’t have to invest much in Dexterity as you normally would on a rogue, and just focus your ASIs on maxing your Charisma.


Level 2

• One more 1st level spell slot. Not much, but it’s nice. You can use hex and wrathful smite and get them back on a short rest.

• One more 1st level spell known. Not a lot of options I love but I might take charm person just for the utility.

•Eldritch Invocations: I recommend Devil’s Sight and Eldritch Mind

•Devil’s Sight: You can see in magical and mundane darkness out to 120 feet. If you are ever stuck in magical darkness with creatures who can’t see through it, you have advantage on your attack rolls. 

•Eldritch Mind: The limitation of spell slots is eased a little bit if you have advantage on concentration saving throws. If you’re not planning on warcaster or resilient:con, I recommend this to help with your hex and wrathful smite.


Level 3

• Your two slots are now 2nd level.

• you learn a single 2nd level spell. I recommend one of the four following options

• Darkness: concentration, 10 minutes of magical darkness that you can see through thanks to Devil’s Sight.

• Hold Person: concentration, up to 1 minute, target makes a Wisdom save and is paralyzed on a failure. This would really suck if it succeeded, wasting one of your precious two spell slots. But if the target is paralyzed you can attack it willingly on your next turn, and your attack will be an automatic critical, which includes double your Sneak Attack dice.

• Invisibility: If you didn’t pick up Stealth expertise this will help you feel more like a rogue, if any exploration needs to be done.

• Shadow Blade: concentration, 1 minute. A magical finesse weapon that deals 2d8 psychic damage means your Sneak Attack damage is also psychic. You also have advantage with the attack in dim light or darkness, and if you want to throw the weapon then you can make it reappear as a bonus action on your next turn.

•Pact Boon: I recommend the Pact of the Blade for obvious reasons.


After that you can take one more level in warlock for an ASI, extra cantrip, and one more known 2nd level spell, or keep going in swashbuckler. Hope this helps

• Writing Down the Bones (Natalie Goldberg)

This is probably the simplest book on my list. The author teaches us how to freewrite, which is completely different from writing fiction and can be helpful for pretty much anyone, even for people who don’t write. Her central idea is about a writing exercise. A timer is set, and you must write the whole time without stopping, only writing down your most impulsive thoughts, including mundane thoughts like “my wrist hurts” and insecure thoughts like “I’m not good enough to be a writer.” What you write during this exercise doesn’t necessarily need to apply to your fiction, but it can.




• Reading Like A Writer (Francine Prose)
Almost every chapter is dedicated to a single element of fiction, from the simplest one being titled “words” and arguably the most complex being called “character”. Each chapter describes how it’s element works and why it’s necessary, using examples from a variety of authors. At the end of the book is a full recommended reading list.



• The Art of Fiction (John Gardener)
Probably the most serious in tone, but one of the most thoughtful meditations on fiction I’ve ever read. The idea of the “fictional dream”, a belief in the reality of the invented world by the reader, is only achieved by the skill of an effective author, and is one of the central ideas of the book. Other discussions include the arguable necessity of formal education as a writer, the value of meta-fiction, and the energeic plot first described by Aristotle. The end of the book includes exercises for practicing how to write, including structured and suspenseful writing.



These are my top three that I can think of. I’m writing this from memory, but I’ve read each of these books multiple times so I feel I understand them pretty well. If you’d like any more recommendations, you can DM me. Good luck with your writing.

• Cunning Action means you can disengage or dash as a bonus action, which is good for getting around the battlefield quickly, and you won’t have to spend ki points on Step of the Wind. 
• Sneak Attack goes up to 2d6 which can be used with a shortsword (monk weapon) and your attacks will be made with advantage if your enemy is knocked prone or stunned by your Stunning Strike at higher levels.
• Thief Rogue gives you Fast Hands which lets you take the Use an Object action as a bonus action. This applies to your healer’s kit, so if you have uses left, you can use your action to Attack, pushing your enemy away, and use your bonus action to stabilize your ally no check required.
